message.content: The description model already covers the kernel and contract, but there's a useful analytic refinement worth recording: with v' = v − 0.5·(p@v), the reference output is y_ref = p@v' = p@v − 0.5·(p@v)·(Σp) = 0.5·(p@v), since Σp = 1. So the reference norm is exactly half the norm of the float64 softmax-weighted value vector — this directly quantifies claim c2 and helps the Experimenter decide whether the 0.001·√32 floor dominates.

message.reasoning_content: The description model is already recorded; claims c1, c2 lack evidence. I'm Describer — nothing new to describe. I could add a refined description note: that the reference norm can be estimated analytically: y_ref = p@v' = p@v - 0.5(p@v)(p@1)... actually v' = v - 0.5*(p@v) broadcast, so y_ref = p@v - 0.5*(p@v)*(sum p) = 0.5*(p@v). So reference norm = 0.5*||p@v||₂ — useful quantification. Record that update, noting it affects c2.
